claims.statement: `.specify/memory/constitution.md` is the repository's single ratified source of core principles governing Frontend Apps, Backend Services, and AI Agents, and it is versioned semver-style with a change log at the top of the file recording every amendment and rationale.

The constitution currently stands at v2.8.0 (ratified 2026-03-08, last amended 2026-11-07), and the `[CURRENT]` marker at the end of the version-history block is the authoritative signal for which amendment is latest.

Constitution amendments must follow the file's Governance procedure: a proposal documenting rationale, impact and migration plan; review and formal approval; a version bump where MAJOR signals a principle change, MINOR a guidance addition and PATCH a clarification; and alignment of existing code within one release cycle.

A deviation from the constitution requires explicit human approval and a documented rationale, whereas a spec or plan may deviate from itself and simply be updated — this is the one asymmetry in the spec-driven lifecycle, so an AI assistant meeting an apparent task/constitution conflict must stop and ask rather than choose silently.

"No Vibe Coding" is a named AI Assistant Constraint requiring the assistant to always refer to the current `plan.md` and `spec.md` before writing code, with deviations requiring explicit documentation and approval — mirroring the constitution's own amendment discipline.

The Identity Provider boundary is a hard trust line: a validated, signed JWT is treated as proof the IdP already evaluated and satisfied Conditional Access and MFA, so the application must never re-implement MFA, CA checks or raw credential verification, and its authentication responsibility is limited to cryptographic token validation (signature and `iss`/`aud`/`azp`/`exp`/`nbf` claims), with authorization remaining the application's own responsibility.

The Behavior-Descriptive Identifiers principle bans requirement/specification IDs (e.g. `FR-###`, `SC-###`, `T-###`, `US#`) from code identifiers such as files, modules and exported symbols; the IDs belong in a traceability comment on the artifact, which is the one explicit exception to the prohibition on WHAT-comments.

Constitution v2.5.0 records a scoped, bounded accepted exception to the Frontend performance-budgeting rule (2-second time-to-interactive on simulated 3G) for the mcm-app web client's cold load only; it covers residual framework weight, leaves the principle's JavaScript-lazy-loading clause in force, and is bounded by a committed 2,000,000-byte budget whose own text still describes an entry-chunk maximum while the enforcing gate measures the cold-load total — a divergence none of the later amendments, including v2.8.0, has corrected.

The bounded web cold-load exception is enforced by `scripts/check-web-bundle-budget.mjs` through the `bundle-budget` Nx target as a committed 2,000,000-byte ceiling that feature 087 repointed from the `entry-*` chunk to the **cold-load total** — the sum of every script the worst exported page loads, read from the exported HTML — measured at 1,892,065 B on the SDK 57 baseline against the constitution's own exception clause, which still describes an entry-chunk maximum and cites 1,762,630 B. The same gate also asserts that deferred assistant-runtime packages are absent from the entry chunk and that server-only code is absent from every client chunk.

Beyond principles, the constitution binds per-stack technology baselines and the monorepo directory structure — fixing language, framework, data-access library, container images, Nx-first task invocation, naming conventions and test placement for Backend Services, Frontend Apps and the AI Agents layer — so non-compliance is remedied by a constitution amendment or a scoped exception rather than a local convention.

The constitution's TDD mandate includes a mandatory RED-then-GREEN checkpoint format for every test task, with a Verify RED command whose expected failure output must be non-zero — a test that cannot be verified RED is not a TDD test.

Constitution v2.6.0 is a MINOR, stack-guidance-only amendment that advances the frontend baseline from Expo SDK 56 to Expo SDK 57 (React Native 0.86, React 19.2); it redefines no principle, and it was drafted in the same pull request as the dependency bump it authorises, per the rule that a version the constitution names must be amended with human approval in the change that moves it.

Only a stack element the constitution names *with a version* forces an amendment when it moves; a library named without a version does not. The frontend stack section names Tamagui and `@mcm/design-system` as the UI/styling engine but pins no version for it, so a Tamagui major is not a constitutional change, whereas the Expo SDK/native runtime, the container images and the toolchain lines are version-named and are.

Beyond principles and stack baselines the constitution carries the architecture diagrams that are the canonical picture of the runtime topology: two C4 container diagrams (multi-frontend/multi-service, and the additive AI-agents layer) and three auth-flow sequence diagrams (login, backend resource access, agent auth), the last of which specifies the RFC 8693 run-scoped subject-token exchange and downscoped backend token that keep token custody with the BFF.

Constitution v2.7.0 is a MINOR, stack-guidance-only amendment that advances the document-database baseline to `mongodb/mongodb-community-server:9.0-ubi9` (MongoDB 9.0 on Red Hat UBI 9), and it records in the changelog that the image the document had named until then, `8.2.6-ubuntu2204-slim`, was stale — `8.0.8-ubi9` is what actually ran. It redefines no principle, was operator-approved, and landed in the same pull request as the compose-file change it authorises.

A version the constitution names can itself be stale, so a version-named line is not proof of what runs: the constitution's document-database image had named a tag the stacks never ran (corrected as part of the amendment that moved the line), and the BFF API line named `node:24.14.1-alpine3.23` while the image built on `24.22.1` — a correction v2.8.0 made without touching the separate Frontend stack `JavaScript Runtime` line. A version-named line must be compared against the manifest, the compose files and the lockfile before being treated as deployed truth.

Constitution compliance is operationalized per feature through a mandatory **Constitution Check** gate in every `plan.md` (the template's wording: "GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design."), which gives each principle a row with a status and how it is satisfied. Feature 081's plan is a worked example: it marks the Expo SDK line and the document-database image line as AMENDMENT REQUIRED, each naming the story that amends it, and marks the Tamagui line PASS because the constitution names that library but no version of it.

The constitution's unversioned "UI / Design System" line asserts Tamagui is "wired runtime-only by default (the Tamagui babel/metro compiler plugins are optional optimisations)", and that behavioural claim was inaccurate from feature 015 onward, which enabled `@tamagui/babel-plugin`. Feature 081 US10 restored the line's accuracy by code rather than by amendment: Tamagui 3 removed the Babel plugin, and its replacement `@tamagui/metro-plugin` 3.0.x was measured to lower some web modules to static class names without emitting their CSS while saving no bytes (entry chunk 1,881,353 B with it versus 1,881,066 B without, against the 2,000,000 B budget), so no Tamagui compiler is wired and `frontend/mcm-app/babel.config.js` runs no Tamagui plugin.

The constitution's Backend Services stack names `medi-rs` as the mandated mediator library for routing commands, queries and events from the API layer to the application-layer handler, but `backend/mc-service` ships no mediator crate: `router::build()` constructs one handler per operation over the repository traits and packs them into `AppState`, so dispatch is a direct method call on that struct. The divergence is recorded in `docs/MCM-Architecture.md` as a tracked backlog item rather than resolved by an amendment, so a constitutionally named library can be absent from the running system while the version history reads as current.

The constitution's amendment procedure is drafted through the Spec Kit constitution command (`.github/agents/speckit.constitution.agent.md`, mirrored as `.claude/skills/speckit-constitution/SKILL.md`), which loads the existing constitution, applies the MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH rule — MAJOR for a principle or governance removal or redefinition, MINOR for a new section or materially expanded guidance, PATCH for clarifications — and carries a consistency-propagation checklist that pushes the change into the dependent templates, including `.specify/templates/plan-template.md` and its spec and tasks siblings.

Feature 081 codifies the same-PR amendment rule as its governance requirement FR-015: where the governing constitution names a version the feature changes (the platform SDK and native runtime, the document-database image), the amendment MUST land in the same pull request as the change it authorises and with human approval; because the constitution names the UI styling library without a version, that story (US10) needs no amendment.

The constitution names the document-database image by *tag* (`mongodb/mongodb-community-server:9.0-ubi9`), while the compose files pin that tag to a digest that is re-resolved whenever upstream rebuilds the image: the production cutover ran `sha256:2cb58a8d…` and the current pin is `sha256:3d40c6fa…`, both the same mongod 9.0.4. A digest refresh inside the named tag is ordinary image maintenance and requires no amendment; only a change to the named tag does. A same-version rebuild can nevertheless change what the security gate sees: the `sha256:3d40c6fa…` UBI 9.8 rebuild shipped a fixed `ca-certificates` and discharged the `CVE-2026-114406` allowlist entry, so the exact digest — not the named tag — determines what runs.

A constitution line can break for a reason that is neither a version number nor a library: the Backend-for-Frontend line described a mechanism (`app.json` web output `"output": "server"`) whose meaning changed on Expo SDK 58 to per-request rendering rather than the prerendered pages plus API routes the app needs, so feature 087's FR-024 amended both the framework baseline and that line together — which is why an upgrade plan must sweep the whole stack section, not only the lines whose text contains a version number.

The constitution names Tamagui without a version, so no amendment is required when it moves, but version discipline for it is enforced elsewhere by `scripts/__tests__/tamagui-version-lockstep.guard.test.mjs`: every `tamagui` / `@tamagui/*` specifier in `frontend/mcm-app/package.json` and `packages/design-system/package.json` must be one exact version with both manifests agreeing, the lock must hold a single resolved `@tamagui/core` and `@tamagui/web`, the removed v2 `@tamagui/babel-plugin` must be named by neither manifest nor `babel.config.js`, and every Tamagui update must resolve to one Renovate group so the bot cannot propose half of the set.

The constitution's monorepo directory tree carries approved deviations as well as rules: it lists `openwiki/` as the generated, OKF-formatted agent-facing knowledge wiki, deliberately kept outside the human-owned `docs/` so that the ownership rule stays enforceable — everything under `openwiki/` may be regenerated by a tool, everything under `docs/` is human-owned, and nesting the wiki inside `docs/` would put generator-rewritable files beside the operator runbooks.

The bundle gate's inline-script assertion and the web content-security-policy cannot disagree: the gate reads `INLINE_SCRIPT_HASHES` from `frontend/mcm-app/web-security-headers.js` through `createRequire`, hashes every inline `<script>` body exactly as the browser would, and fails an unlisted one offline while printing the `'sha256-…'` value the reviewed allowlist would need rather than granting permission to add it. The Nx `bundle-budget` target invokes the gate with `--require-maps` so a missing source map fails loudly instead of silently narrowing the check to the byte budget, and the web cold-load performance E2E keeps its own transferred-JS ceiling (1,950 KB) in step with the same 2,000,000-byte figure.

The gate's module lists are its extension points: `DEFERRED_PACKAGES` names the assistant-runtime packages (`zod`, `graphql`, `@copilotkit/`, `@ag-ui/`, `rxjs`, `@bufbuild/protobuf`, `text-encoding`, `web-streams-polyfill`) that the principle's lazy-loading clause requires to stay out of the entry chunk, and `SERVER_ONLY` names `src/bff-server/` and `luxon`. The escape hatch beside them, `SERVER_ONLY_EXEMPT`, is empty by design because item #566 relocated the browser's axios transport to the Utils-Layer, so `src/bff-server/` now means server-only without exception; a future entry there is deliberately two-sided — it must be paired with a `@client-safe: <reason>` marker in the module itself, which `scripts/check-no-server-imports.mjs` reads — and one without the other is an unexplained hole in whichever gate lacks it.

The bundle gate guards itself against reporting clean when it should not: `--selftest` proves the fail and clean paths on synthetic trees, and `scripts/__tests__/check-web-bundle-budget.test.mjs` covers the specific cases where a plausible gate reads clean — no entry chunk at all, two entry chunks, a deferred package back in the entry chunk while the byte budget still passes, server code in the deferred chunk, a missing source map, two chunks that fit apart but not together, and an unlisted inline script.

Constitution v2.8.0 (2026-11-07) is a MINOR, stack-guidance-only amendment that advances the framework baseline to Expo SDK 58 with React Native 0.88 and React 19.3, moves the BFF web output from `"output": "server"` to `"output": "static"` with `apiRoutes: true` on the `expo-router` plugin so pages stay prerendered at build time while API routes keep running in the same Node process, and corrects the BFF API container's stale `node:24.14.1-alpine3.23` line to `node:24.22.1-alpine3.23`. It redefines no principle, was approved by the operator on 2026-11-08, and landed in the same pull request as the SDK move it authorises (FR-024, task T048).

`frontend/mcm-app/app.json` sets the Expo web output to `"static"` and configures the `expo-router` plugin with `apiRoutes: true` and `asyncRoutes: { "web": false }`; `asyncRoutes.web` is written out explicitly because SDK 58's plugin with no options turns it on, and a page that throws during rendering fails `expo export` rather than shipping a broken page.

The bundle gate's cold-load measurement on the SDK 58 export was 1,926,163 B of the 2,000,000 B budget (96.3%, 73,837 B spare) on the worst of 17 exported pages — +34,342 B (+1.8%) over the SDK 57 baseline of 1,892,065 B — with the budget itself unchanged, so the exception's remaining headroom is under one ordinary feature.

The repository's enforced Node requirement is not any version the constitution names but the `engines.node` floor in the root manifest (`>=22.13`, set from pnpm 11's own engines and deliberately not lowered when pnpm 12 declared only `>=18`), which `scripts/check-toolchain-consistency.mjs` checks every workflow `node-version:` and Dockerfile `FROM node:<v>` pin against — so the constitution's Frontend stack `JavaScript Runtime` line still reading `Node.js Latest LTS (v24.14.1)` is neither the floor nor what CI or the BFF image runs.

Feature 087's plan uses the same Constitution Check gate as every other feature and shows the harder case: both the framework-baseline row and the BFF output-mode row are marked AMENDMENT REQUIRED under the single v2.8.0 amendment — the second because its literal text would mean per-request rendering on SDK 58 — with a second, post-design pass appended under the same heading rather than a fresh one.
